bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your AFL Umpire Salary: Hourly to Annual

Whether you are a field umpire, boundary umpire, or goal umpire, understanding how your **AFL umpire salary** translates from an hourly rate to an annual figure is essential for budgeting, tax planning, and comparing job offers. This guide uses the standard 38-hour week formula, explains casual loading and superannuation, and references official sources from the Fair Work Commission and the Australian Taxation Office.

### The Hourly to Annual Formula

The basic conversion is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full-time employee working 38 hours each week, 38 hours is the standard. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, which equals $1,004.90 per week or $52,254.80 per year.

If you are a casual AFL umpire, you may receive a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate, giving $33.05 per hour for a casual employee. The formula remains the same: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $62,706.80 per year before tax and super.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage and modern award rates. The National Minimum Wage applies to award-free employees. From 1 July 2026, the weekly rate is $1,004.90 for 38 hours. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award with minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates. For AFL umpires, specific rates may be set by an enterprise agreement or a modern award such as the *Supported Employment Services Award* or *Miscellaneous Award*, but the conversion method is identical.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation on Top

Casual loading is an additional 25% on the base hourly rate. It is not included in the base rate; you add it when calculating your gross pay. For example, if your base rate is $26.44, your casual rate is $33.05. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave.

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a casual employee earning $62,706.80 per year, the employer contributes an additional $7,524.82 into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra benefit.

### Fortnightly Pay and Tax Estimates

Many employers pay fortnightly. For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80. For a casual AFL umpire, fortnightly gross pay would be $2,410.80 ($1,205.40 per week).

Tax is calculated on your gross annual salary using the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a full-time employee earning $52,254.80, tax would be approximately $7,676.44 plus Medicare $1,045.10, leaving a take-home pay of about $43,533.26 per year. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

### AFL Umpire Salary Context

While the exact **AFL umpire salary** varies by experience, level, and match type, the conversion principles are universal. The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database contains minimum rates for various classifications, but AFL umpires are typically covered by enterprise agreements rather than awards. The National Minimum Wage provides a baseline for casual workers. For a casual umpire working 38 hours per week at the minimum casual rate of $33.05 per hour, the annual equivalent is $62,706.80. This is before tax and super. For a more precise calculation, check your agreement or award using the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Summary

To convert your hourly AFL umpire salary to annual:
- Multiply your hourly rate by 38 (hours per week) and then by 52 (weeks per year).
- Add 25% casual loading if applicable.
- Remember that superannuation is paid on top at 12%.
- Use the [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading.

This estimate assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a guide, not a determination of your pay or tax. Always refer to your award or agreement for exact conditions.
